html:
The Martuthunira are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Pilbara coast of Western Australia, around the mouth of the Fortescue River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Ngarluma to the east, the Kurrama inland and the Nhuwala to the west. Sheep stations and pearling spread along this coast from the 1860s, after the founding of Roebourne, and took much of their land and labour.

Their language is now extinct. The last fluent speaker, Algy Paterson, died in 1995. From 1980 he worked with the linguist Alan Dench to record it, and most of what is known of Martuthunira comes from their work.
